class_guess: Skelet 1-like Class 2: binary down-counter on a list of (10)^p(01)^q pairs with overflow re-pairing (SBCv6 TM21 family)
summary: Binary down-counter on a list of (10)^p(01)^q pairs; overflow re-pairs the list (TM21-like). 7 rules validated.
mechanism: Tape: (10)^h, marker 11001, then pairs (10)^p (01)^q, each ending in a digit block 0001 (=1) or 0010 (=0).
Each cycle (3 short bounces + 1 long sweep) subtracts 1 from that binary number; pairs the borrow passes get p+1, q-1.
At 0, End adds a tail; at the next 0, Overflow re-pairs the list and adds a pair (net ~1 per 2 epochs: width ~ t^0.5).

rules.name: Dec
rules.cases: k=0..L-1 (borrow chain); b_i>=1, q>=1; any h mod 4; R = remaining pairs + any tail

rules.name: DecMerge
rules.cases: q hits 0 on a 1->0 digit: fuse with next pair; last pair fuses into tail: (10)^p (01) 0001 (10)^t 1 -> (10)^(p+t+3) 1

rules.name: End
rules.cases: all digits 0, no tail; b_i>=1, q>=1. q=0 (EndLast): last pair becomes tail (10)^(p+4) 1, validated 36/36

rules.name: Ov
rules.cases: all digits 0, tail present; a_1>=1; new counter value 2^(L+1)-2

rules.name: X1
rules.cases: End with the last two q = 1 (seen once, step 251,973,021)

rules.name: X2
rules.cases: all digits 0 with tail (101)^2(01)^k; returns to the normal family

template.diff: 8 of 11 defined transitions differ under the best state renaming (no mirror); Sk1like_TC_v1/v2 machines differ in 8-9
template.note: Same architecture (pair list + counter sweeps + overflow re-pairing + finite tail states = TM21's LIncs/Ov/LH1-3), but not its shapes: from TM21's init config this machine halts in 4,539 steps. Sk1like_TC (eventual cycler via native_compute) doesn't fit.

strategy:
Copy TM21's skeleton: pair-list datatype with digit tags; Dec/End/Ov/merge/X1/X2 as follow-chains of es/ind sweep lemmas over (10)^p(01)^q blocks (Longitudinal sideRLs like TM21's LIncs if sweeps are batched).
Nonhalt via multistep_nonhalt + progress_nonhalt_cond with an LWF-style invariant: every q_j exceeds the borrows it gets before its digit next flips 0->1, plus a 3-state tail automaton (none / (10)^t 1 / (101)^2(01)^k).
risks: Invariant: the far end has small margins (a far q shrinks by 3 per 2 epochs); excluding a bad merge (q->0 on a 0->1 digit) needs exact far-end bookkeeping. Simulation only so far (2^48 abstract cycles).
Size: TM21-style proof plus a tail automaton and 7 rule shapes, probably 15-30 KB.
Class 1 neighbour is being mined from a numbered Sk1 list; unknown whether that list covers Class 2 (memo Q3).

checkpoint_questions.text: zoom_cycles_annotated: rows 8,319 to 17,139 (between the yellow RE-PAIR bands); each row is the tape at the start of one count-down step. A pair = a run of 10s (blue) then a run of 01s (orange); its digit block = the next 4 cells (purple), 0001 = 1, 0010 = 0. Expected: each purple block stays on the same 4 cells all the way down; only its one light (1) cell moves, one cell left or right, when the digit flips (0001 ↔ 0010): in pair 1's block every row (the zigzag), in pair 2's every other row, and in pair 3's once, at row 10,419. At row 13,983 pair 3 turns into the teal tail. Meanwhile each blue→orange border jumps 2 cells right on some rows: pair 1's on every row, pair 2's on every other row. The magnified box at the top shows one such step cell by cell. Is that what you see? (In Fig 1, zoomed far out, the purple blocks are the vertical edges and the borders the slanted ones.)
checkpoint_questions.note: The purple block is a coherent column, but it shifts internally (light vs dark purple) and translates by one cell partway down; the single-cell checkerboard columns are what Q2 explains. So 'keeps its columns' is not literally true.

checkpoint_questions.text: zoom_cycles_annotated: the two yellow RE-PAIR bands, above rows 8,319 and 19,436. Re-pairing = the tape is regrouped into new pairs and the counter restarts (here at 6); it happens when the counter (right margin) hits 0 for the second time. At the first 0 the step is End instead: it raises the counter (0 → 1 at row 6,366; 0 → 3 at row 13,983) and changes the right end, and the two Ends differ: '+ tail' (row 6,366) adds a 3-cell teal tail after the last pair, while 'pair 3 → tail' (row 13,983) absorbs pair 3 into the tail. Across each band, black dashed lines carry the old blue→orange borders down and purple dotted lines the middles of the old purple blocks. Expected: the dashed lines end on the new purple blocks of pairs 1 and 2, and the dotted lines end 1 cell left of the new borders of pairs 2 and 3 (pair 1's starts next to the old gold marker), so the two kinds of column swap roles. Re-pairing also adds a pair: the new pair 3's orange run takes over the old teal tail, and its purple block (the rightmost) sits just past where the tail ended, so no line leads to it. Is that what you see? (In Fig 1 each swap is a row where the vertical and slanted edges kink.)
checkpoint_questions.note: Black dashed lines carry the old blue→orange borders down; purple dotted lines carry the old purple blocks down: that explains the checkerboard.

checkpoint_questions.text: Fig 2: the long sweeps go deep, shallow, then medium as the counter goes 12 → 11 → 10 → 9. Does the sweep depth read as the borrow chain of a binary down-counter?
